A bicycle gear system is a mechanical application of **torque and revolutions**, designed to allow a rider to maintain an efficient cadence (pedaling speed) while overcoming different levels of resistance, such as steep inclines or high-speed flats.

The system operates through a relationship between two main components: the **chainring** (the gears at the pedals) and the **cassette** (the gears on the rear wheel). These are linked by a chain.

### How the Mechanics Work
The core principle is the ratio of teeth between these two sets of gears. When you shift gears, you are changing the mechanical advantage of your "leverage."
